key_quotes: Existing and emergent smart city technology has the potential to be used by the UK military to gain significant advantages in their operations within urban environments. || The military will increasingly operate in an environment of pervasive surveillance. This will reduce their ability to operate undetected. || The concept of smart city is an evolving process in which cities aim to become more 'liveable' and resilient and, hence, able to respond more quickly to new challenges [as they] bring together hard infrastructure, social capital including local skills and community institutions and [digital] technologies to fuel sustainable economic development.
policy_relevance: Provides extensive military recommendations: develop urban database, train cultural advisors, invest in cyber capabilities, explore autonomous vehicles, and adapt force structure for urban operations.

title: Territorialising the cloud or clouding the territory? Volumetric vulnerabilities and the militarised conjunctures of Singapore’s smart city-state
thesis: The volumetric characteristics of cloud computing create new expressions of territoriality that reveal vulnerabilities and militarised conjunctures in Singapore's smart city-state.
key_quotes: The overlap of 'city' and 'state' causes matters of national security to be urban as much as they are national concerns. The defensive role of the military has caused Singapore to become a 'key theoretical site for applying a governmentality optic, given the contiguous relationship with sovereign nation-state-power'. || if you just look at the capacity on the public clouds' workload running everywhere – core, edge, and very distributed – I think that makes the problem around threat detection and threat remediation very much more acute, because your attack surface is therefore much, much, much wider. || MINDEF/SAF can leverage our digital factory rapidly to meet operational needs, I think that is something we can offer the smart city conversation on how to develop products that meet changing needs in a very rapid way.
policy_relevance: Discusses the need for geofencing and data localisation strategies to territorialise cloud data; recommends policy reviews for cloud security in smart city contexts; highlights the role of digital factories and public-private partnerships in managing volumetric vulnerabilities; emphasises the importance of civil-military fusion in national security strategy.

title: Digital cities and their commercial aesthetics: The celebration of monarchy in Bangkok
thesis: Digital urban infrastructure in Bangkok facilitates cheap and efficient circulation of royal visual propaganda, reinforcing monarchical authority and normalizing urban inequality.
key_quotes: This article argues that the expanding role of digital urban infrastructure in Bangkok has revitalised a visual aesthetic designed to uphold royal authority. || Digital infrastructure provided a cheap and horizontally far-reaching mode of communication which replicated pre-existing images. || The everyday encounters with images of the monarchy in commercial spaces and online platforms thus serve as an intimate and unavoidable imposition of royal influence.
policy_relevance: None

title: Tweets of surveillance: Traffic, Twitter, and securitization in Beirut, Lebanon
thesis: The Twitter account for Beirut's Traffic Management Center illustrates how social media technology serves as a portal for state securitization and legitimacy, while also enabling citizen challenges to state authority.
key_quotes: The Twitter profile page for Beirut's Traffic Management Center shows a control room with policemen sitting in front of numerous monitors that display live feeds from the city's traffic cameras. It is an image highlighting not merely the state's ability to harness technology in the management of vehicular mobility, but also how technology itself becomes a terrain for the securitization of urban public space. || In broadcasting the state's capacity to remotely monitor traffic, these images suggest the ubiquity – made possible by smart technologies – of the state surveillance of public life. || By making it possible for citizens to 'watch from below,' the technology of Twitter becomes a political terrain, a platform for the social struggle over the notions and practices of security.
policy_relevance: The paper suggests that smart technologies in urban governance can both reinforce state authority and enable citizen contestation, highlighting the need for transparent and accountable use of surveillance technologies in public space.

title: Roads Infrastructure Digital Twin: A Step Toward Smarter Cities Realization
thesis: Proposes a Digital Twin Box for roads infrastructure to enable smart city applications, including object detection and recognition for security, tourism, and autonomous driving.
key_quotes: The outcome of the latter step would be of utmost importance to many other services and domains such as national security. || Also, the national security authorities can also use the platform to search for a suspicious person/car just by using their picture/its plate number to see the different places visited by that person/car, respectively. || The combination and fusion of all gathered and processed data will give a better understanding of the contextual circumstances when accessing the data. The resulting database would be of great importance for many other services and domains such as tourism, insurance and national security.
policy_relevance: None

title: A systematic literature review of open innovation in the public sector: comparing barriers and governance strategies of digital and non-digital open innovation
thesis: Compares barriers and governance strategies between digital and non-digital open innovation in the public sector, finding relational barriers dominate non-digital OI and capacity/technical barriers dominate digital OI.
key_quotes: The results of this review indicate that relational barriers are relatively more influential for non-digital OI. ... On the other hand, capacity- and technical-related barriers emerge as the major challenge for digital OI. || Such transformation from relational barriers to capacity- and technical-related barriers indicates that digital technologies may reduce the need for direct government-stakeholder interaction that is usually full of tensions, but simultaneously they bring about new capacity-related challenges to steer the technologies. || Our review also reveals that to remove the barriers of OI, governance strategies need to be appropriately adopted by governments.
policy_relevance: Discusses governance strategies for open innovation: political commitment, intermediaries, top-down mandates for public-public OI, supportive/persuasive strategies for offline citizen participation, reward/review for online participation, and data quality management/legal frameworks for digital public-private OI.

title: CollectiveOS Exobody Node Program (IX-1): A Comprehensive Technical and Operational Analysis of the First Civilian-Legal Telepresence Platform
thesis: The IX-1 Exobody Node Program is a civilian-legal telepresence platform that rejects militarization and surveillance capitalism, using certified hardware and immutable logging to ensure safety and accountability.
key_quotes: The IX-1 emerges as a distinct third vector, rejecting both militarization and surveillance capitalism in favor of a new paradigm: Human-Centric Augmentation. || It asserts that the future of robotics need not be defined by the lethal autonomy of the battlefield or the privacy-eroding surveillance of the smart city. || The IX-1 is not a monolithic robot; it is a distributed 'exosystem' comprising three distinct physical domains—Neural, Ground, and Air—linked by a unified software nervous system.
policy_relevance: None explicitly beyond promoting civilian-legal certification and compliance frameworks for robotics.

title: Intelligent 5G Networks Designed and Integrated for Globalized Operations (INDIGO)
Algorithmic Governance and the International Politics of Big Tech
thesis: Algorithmic governance by Big Tech creates new private authorities and mediates state-corporate relations, requiring IR scholars to engage with these issues.
key_quotes: Google’s image recognition algorithms have helped inform target selection for US drone strikes in the 'War on Terror' (Amoore 2020). || In 'algorithmic governance,' deference to automated decision-making makes algorithms 'a source and factor of social order' (Just and Latzer 2017, 246). || The opacity of algorithms makes it difficult to know precisely when one is being influenced by algorithms and then to identify specific harms.
policy_relevance: Discusses need for regulation (antitrust, privacy, speech), corporate responsibility, and international frameworks like GDPR and Digital Services Act. Highlights challenges of legitimating Big Tech's private authority.

title: 영국 경찰기관의 빅 데이터 활용 관리와 정책 시사점에 관한 연구
thesis: Examines UK police big data systems and integration efforts, drawing policy implications for Korean police.
key_quotes: random hit rates were less than 1%, intelligence-led hit rates were 5%, and algorithm-based predictions were 10 times more accurate than random and 2 times more accurate than intelligence-led predictions. || The integration of databases was intended to enable qualitative and quantitative improvements in Big Data analysis, allowing law enforcement agencies to effectively deal with organized, cross-regional, and cyber crimes. || If police big data were to be fully integrated with the data owned by GCHQ, it would have significant implications for individual privacy and human rights.
policy_relevance: Recommends establishment of a national data strategy, a central control tower for big data, and legal reforms to balance efficiency with privacy rights.

title: Post-racial politics, pre-emption and in/security
thesis: Predictive policing and counter-terrorism algorithms mobilise post-racial logics that renew racial oppression while appearing race-neutral, making security indistinguishable from insecurity.
key_quotes: PredPol software was developed... using algorithms used for predicting earthquake aftershocks to anticipate the location of crime 'hot spots'... Brantingham was motivated to develop PredPol through his original Pentagon-funded work, which forecasted battlefield casualties in Iraq. Other projects included research funded by the US Department of Defense which attempted to model 'gang' violence in California via Iraqi insurgent attacks (González, 2015). || algorithmic systems involved in the calculus of risk for state securitization are racializing assemblages. The features that matter in identifying a future terrorist and determining levels of threat operate... upon logics of racialisation that are encoded into specific computational parameters. Algorithms do not become racialised when encountering data imbued with elements of sociopolitical difference but rather mobilise logics of racialisation in order to process data assemblages (p. 31). || Policing does not have a 'racist history'. Policing makes race and is inextricable from it. Algorithms cannot 'code out' race from American policing because race is an originary policing technology, just as policing is a bedrock racializing technology.
policy_relevance: Critiques the UK's Prevent and Channel counter-terrorism programmes, highlighting their racialized and pre-emptive nature, and the way they normalise surveillance and intervention on Muslim populations. Recommends recognising the in/security and containment logic of the War on Terror.

title: Embodied Data, Shifting Perspective: Future Wake and the Politics of Predictive Policing
thesis: Examines the artistic project Future Wake that uses predictive algorithms to predict police killings, shifting focus from offenders to victims, to critically reflect on the politics and logics of predictive policing and algorithmic violence.
key_quotes: Predictive policing is a form of big data surveillance in which historical crime data is analysed for the purpose of predicting in which geographical areas there is an increased likelihood that crime will occur. || What data law enforcement collects, their methods for analyzing and interpreting it, and the way it informs their practice are all part of a fundamentally social process. Characterizing predictive models as “just math,” and fetishizing computation as an objective process, obscures the social side of algorithmic decision-making. || By transforming abstract data points into faces, Future Wake destabilizes this neutrality and objectivity of data, and highlights how real people are impacted by such datafied predictions.
policy_relevance: None explicitly, but calls for transparency and critical democratic inspection of AI systems.

title: Optimization of the homicide predictive classification algorithm: a study applied to the military police of Minas Gerais state, Brazil
thesis: Optimizes a Homicide Predictive Classification algorithm for the Military Police of Minas Gerais to enhance predictive accuracy and support focused deterrence strategies.
key_quotes: Unlike COMPAS, which operates as a proprietary recidivism assessment tool with limited transparency, HPC Test 6 offers open mathematical formulations and explicit variable weighting, ensuring reproducibility and being auditable. || Critics point to the opacity of algorithmic processes and the lack of public oversight, which may undermine police legitimacy and deepen public distrust. || As O'Neil (2016) warns, predictive systems reflect the fallibility of their human creators and may inadvertently reinforce social inequalities.
policy_relevance: Recommends integrating additional datasets (prison management, civil registry) and emphasizes transparency, institutional oversight, and focused deterrence strategies.

title: Tackling Delinquency in the Era of Social Credit System: Prospects and Risks
thesis: The Chinese Social Credit System transforms punishment into a diffuse, permanent consequence separated from culpable acts, undermining legal liability institutions.
key_quotes: Основным модусом действия ССК и связанных с ней механизмов контроля является не что иное, как инструментализация человеческого поведения в целях его последующих модификации и прогнозирования, что уже отмечалось в недавней работе американской исследовательницы Ш. Зубофф. || Алгоритмическая архитектура ССК освобождает наказание от безусловной связи с правонарушением, виной, законной мерой и сколь-либо прозрачными процедурами, заставляя субъекта с повышенным вниманием относиться к своим повседневным занятиям и привычкам. || Развивающаяся алгоритмизация этих механизмов влечет превращение субъекта права в 'цифровую личность', перманентно находящуюся под угрозой применения наказания.
policy_relevance: Concludes that risks of the Social Credit System outweigh benefits due to erosion of legal state principles and individual rights guarantees; implies need for caution in implementing similar systems.

title: A Survey of Applicability of Military Data Model Architectures for Smart City Data Consumption and Integration
thesis: Proposes architecture for integrating Smart City data into military information systems using standardized military data models to improve situational awareness.
key_quotes: In these cases, an existing Smart City infrastructure can greatly assist emergency forces like relief units or supporting military forces by providing the data it already has. || The paper discusses how the available data and information from a Smart City infrastructure can be utilized to improve the SA of emergency forces like relief units or the military during an operation in a Smart City environment. || For the integration of the Smart City information into the federated information space we propose to map the IoT information to existing military data models.
policy_relevance: None

title: Neoliberalisation of Security, Austerity and the ‘End of Public Policy’: Governing Crime in Memphis (TN, USA) Through Predictive Policing, Community, Grants and Police ‘Mission Creep’
thesis: The paper argues that neoliberalisation and austerity in Memphis security policymaking lead to the 'end of public policy' as conscious government action, replaced by contradictory patchworks of state intervention/disengagement.
key_quotes: Data analysis and advanced technology provide policymakers and the public an illusion of objectivity, which is particularly appealing in times of fiscal constraint and requests for accountability (Ferguson, 2012, 269; Townsend, 2015). || Predictive policing is the most comprehensive way in which data and algorithms have permeated urban security. A hyper-technological version of hot-spot policing, predictive policing analyses historical spatial patterns of reported crimes and real-time CCTV data to decide where and when police patrols should be deployed with preventive function. || The deployment of cameras in White neighbourhoods versus 'safety zones' in Black neighbourhoods is evidence of the way urban security has become a means to govern and reproduce socio-economic relationships (cf. Simon, 2007; Camp and Heatherton, 2016; Hinton, 2016): reassuring the rich, policing the (racialised) poor.
policy_relevance: The paper warns that austerity-driven security policymaking replaces conscious public policy with contradictory patchworks, and calls for addressing structural root causes of crime. It highlights the inefficiency of militarised policing and the need for social policy investment.

title: Attaining Security Through Algorithms: Perspectives of Refugees and Data Experts
thesis: Refugees and data experts have contrasting perspectives on police risk-scoring algorithms, revealing a double security paradox where refugees are both at risk and perceived as risks, amid concerns about bias, division, and algorithmic opacity.
key_quotes: We develop seemingly smart algorithms, but in reality, they are black boxes and we don't actually know the intricacies of how they operate. This poses all sorts of risks. || The algorithms are perceived to construct further social borders in society and justify extant ideas about marginalized groups. || One of the main concerns related to use of a PRSA or similar algorithmic solutions is that such systems may create further divisions in society based on certain categories that may be related to race, ethnicity, ideology, social class or even appearance.
policy_relevance: Recommends including data subjects' views in algorithmic development and adding transparency to algorithms to increase trust in authorities. Calls for ensuring algorithms are just and fair in mediating diverse experiences.

title: Repressive connectivity and digital resistance: internet shutdowns, speech and networked counterpublics in Manipur
thesis: Internet shutdowns are acts of epistemic violence and infrastructural control that weaponize digital infrastructures to suppress dissent, but also catalyze adaptive resistance and subaltern counterpublics.
key_quotes: Internet shutdowns, algorithmic censorship and data extraction exemplify what this article terms repressive connectivity: a logic in which digital infrastructures serve as instruments of surveillance, exclusion and epistemic control (Deibert 2022; Zuboff 2019). || The shift from democratic pluralism to a technocratic and opaque regime of control suggests not merely a regulatory overreach but an epistemic transformation – where knowledge production, dissent and public deliberation are increasingly shaped by logics of secrecy, invisibility and algorithmic governance (Pasquale 2015). || Internet shutdowns in this context extend those colonial logics by enacting what Santos calls epistemicide: the erasure, distortion, or silencing of subaltern knowledge through state-engineered disconnection.
policy_relevance: Calls for international legal frameworks to hold states accountable for internet shutdowns as human rights violations, and advocates for epistemic and infrastructural justice, including community-owned mesh networks and encryption tools. References UN HRC Resolution 32/13 and ICCPR General Comment No. 34.

title: Pre-crime, Post-criminology, and the Captivity of Ultramodern Desire
thesis: Hyper-securitization in the ultramodern era, through pre-crime sign-optics and post-criminology sign-exchange values, produces clinical captivity by reducing inter-relatedness through de-vitalization and finalization.
key_quotes: The pre-crime society of Deleuzian control is both a metaphor about and a meditation on the conditions of relational captivity. || The optics of hyper-securitization refer to the cultural signs of dataveillance. || The datafication of subjects and the problematic ontological and epistemological claims of this dataism.
policy_relevance: None. The paper provides a critical diagnosis of hyper-securitization but does not offer specific policy recommendations.

title: Ambivalent Morality: Negotiating the (Neo)Colonial Conditions of Policing at the Urban Margins
thesis: Police officers negotiate neocolonial conditions of predictive policing through ambivalent morality, hybrid discourses that both reinforce and deflect poverty as a source of crime.
key_quotes: We are guided 100% by hard data ["Nos guiamos 100% del dato duro"] (Police Officer, Fieldnotes 07.2022). || Here you can see 'broken windows' theory ["la teoria de la ventana rota"], you know, how Giuliani’s and Bratton’s theory about crime fully works here ["aqui funciona tupido y parejo"] (Professional 2, Fieldnotes 07.2022). || Tell me, how the hell am I going to interfere with that? ["Dime, como chucha voy a intervenir en eso?"] (Officer 3 on Coleros, Fieldnotes 07.2022).
policy_relevance: None

title: Developing CTS 4-o: a CTS research agenda on AI, terrorism and counter-terrorism
thesis: Argues that Critical Terrorism Studies must engage with AI in terrorism and counter-terrorism, exposing how AI-driven security exacerbates inequalities while reifying the status quo.
key_quotes: AI is not merely a neutral technological tool but also a complex sociotechnical system that shapes and is shaped by power dynamics, political interests and security imaginaries. || Despite the narratives of reliability, objectiveness and value-free technology that somewhat hide this issue, AI is trained on data that have been produced by humans, based on societal dynamics. || The use of technology is usually narrated and imagined as the way to achieve 'secure society'... Nonetheless, the questions of whose security, security for whom, and who is a threat and for whom are rarely asked.
policy_relevance: Discusses the EU AI Act and exceptions for counter-terrorism, highlighting how the constructed exceptionality of terrorism permeates AI regulation. Calls for critical scrutiny of AI-driven counter-terrorism policies.

title: Shaping Migrants as Threats: Multilayered Discretion, Criminalization, and Risk Assessment Tools
thesis: Risk assessment tools in Norwegian policing of migration translate European threat frames into local practices, criminalizing migrants through multilayered discretion and net-widening effects.
key_quotes: Through its large Risk Analysis Unit and its Europe-wide network for collating data on border crossings (Frontex Risk Analysis Network), Frontex “exports” risk thinking to member state agencies, reinforcing the threat and security frames in operation on [the] national level, while contributing to the prioritisation of migration controls at the external borders above other tasks. || Risk analysis revealing border vulnerabilities and threats is, therefore, important for supporting decisions about resource allocation at both the EU and Norwegian level. || The way risk and crime predictions are co-constructed and context-dependent also directs our attention to the understandings of crime that different actors and software work with and reproduce in policing.
policy_relevance: The paper critiques the use of risk assessment tools that criminalize migrants and recommends more inclusive approaches aligned with the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child. It highlights the need to evaluate the consequences of preemptive policing and to consider migrant security in risk analysis.

title: Understanding Artificial Intelligence: Fundamentals, Use Cases and Methods for a Corporate AI Journey
thesis: This book provides a comprehensive overview of AI fundamentals, use cases, and methods for corporate AI adoption, emphasizing ethical considerations and strategic implementation.
key_quotes: AI-controlled drones, which not only carry out the flight autonomously, but also independently recognize and fight targets (people and things). || Without Explainable Artificial Intelligence, AI applications remain a black box, making a critical analysis of the underlying processes and the results difficult or impossible. || The goals of the Chinese government can be described in a few words. They want to reward good behavior by citizens and encourage them to stay out of trouble.
policy_relevance: Discusses policy implications such as GDPR, need for ethical guidelines, investment in AI, and the role of government in promoting education and legal frameworks. Recommends a balance between regulation and innovation.

title: Inclusive smart public spaces: insights from Smart Cities and Suburbs
thesis: Explores how smart public spaces can both enhance and challenge inclusivity, using two case studies from the Australian Smart Cities and Suburbs scheme.
key_quotes: The use of information and communication technologies to address the production and management of public spaces is presented as a way of addressing some of these issues and improving the inclusivity of public spaces. || The way that this data from public places is captured, used, and stored can shape the capacity for digital technologies to produce inclusive public space. || Data captured through private sector operators can often be restricted to public access or only be made available to government and other third-party access through fee or licence, effectively privatizing knowledge about public spaces.
policy_relevance: None

title: E-Governance and Ethical AI: Balancing Automation, Privacy, and Human Rights
thesis: AI integration in e-governance enhances public service delivery but raises ethical concerns that require balanced regulatory frameworks to ensure fairness, accountability, and human rights.
key_quotes: AI-driven surveillance tools, such as facial recognition systems, have raised privacy concerns due to potential government overreach and mass data collection. || AI-based decision-making in governance often functions as a 'black-box,' making it difficult to interpret how certain decisions are made. || Algorithmic bias remains a significant challenge, as AI models trained on historical data may reinforce existing societal disparities, leading to discriminatory outcomes in areas such as welfare distribution and law enforcement.
policy_relevance: Discusses legal frameworks (EU AI Act, GDPR, India's DPDP Act) and proposes strategies for ethical AI including transparency, human-in-the-loop, and global collaboration to align AI governance with democratic values.

title: The Classical Liberal Case for Privacy in a World of Surveillance and Technological Change
thesis: Presents a classical liberal case for privacy based on information exchange, limited government, and evolutionary technological change.
key_quotes: We produce a torrent of data even as we do the most trivial activities. ... The digitization of everything has produced digital records of everything. All this information has enormous value. || The classical liberal case for privacy has four elements: the information exchange model of privacy, the protection of privacy against both governments and fellow citizens, a liberal perspective on privacy policy choices, and an understanding of the evolutionary nature of privacy norms and technologies. || Privacy is not simply an absence of information about us in the minds of others; rather it is the control we have over information about ourselves.
policy_relevance: Advocates for limited government intervention and market-based solutions for privacy protection. Criticizes the GDPR for undermining consumer sovereignty and creating perverse data markets. Recommends empowering individuals through education, privacy-enhancing technologies, and strong property rights in data.

title: The Development of Smart Awareness among Ukraine's Youth in Modern Conditions
thesis: Examines the development of smart awareness among Ukrainian youth, finding it remains at an intuitive-practical level despite war-driven acceleration of e-services.
key_quotes: The Smart City is not only about technology. But today, when data is the new 'gold,' in the hands of authoritarian governments or even those who do not know how to manage masses of information, Smart Cities can become entire centers of surveillance, as demonstrated by authoritarian countries. || If the Smart City technology develops within the limits of a democratic society and comprehensively appeals to its residents and local authorities, if it is controlled by people, then yes, I think this is our future. || The existence of video surveillance systems in Ukrainian cities during the occupation of Ukrainian territories made it possible to record the crimes of the Russians in order to initiate future procedural actions.
policy_relevance: Recommends developing citizen competencies for smart consumption, involving residents in smart city discussions, and creating public platforms for idea generation; mentions need for socially responsible institutions.

title: Seeing like an algorithm: operative images and emergent subjects
geography: global (with emphasis on US and China)
thesis: Algorithmic vision reconfigures the image from representational to operational, enabling algorithmic governance that produces emergent subjects through pattern-finding and risk calculus.
key_quotes: The data set has been traced to research papers published by Chinese AI SaaS companies associated with the surveillance techniques used by the Chinese military to target and monitor the activities of Uyghur populations in remote northwest China || Algorithmic vision reveals subjects to power in a mode that requires a new approach towards analyzing the entanglement and invisiblization of the human in automated decision-making systems. || What can be accelerated and increased in prison?... Farocki reveals that this black box of decisions that caused one man to take another's life contained nothing but a human corruption of power.
policy_relevance: Implies need for ethical regulations on future use of personal information and dataset governance; critiques prioritization of surveillance technologies over individual rights.

title: The Impact of Smart City Model on National Security
thesis: Smart city models, while beneficial, create significant national security risks from cyberattacks, requiring technical, political, and societal measures.
key_quotes: Smart cities could help overcome traditional problems of big cities, such as pollution, traffic congestion and administrative corruption. They can stimulate economic productivity, accommodate population growth, and make lives more convenient, but at the same time, they raise many security threats to national security. || Closed source smart city models raise questions regarding security and privacy, from one side the city developer in this model is one company who owns the operation systems, and so has access to all of the information of the cities, knows where is the weaknesses and from where the danger can come. From another side it could also leave a backdoor to have illegal access to information when needed. || The fact that all data would be in the hands of the smart city’s managers can constitute a serious threat to democracy. The local, or the central, government, enjoying full access to citizens’ data, would be able to have full knowledge of their interests, attitudes, preferences and priorities through analyzing data.
policy_relevance: Recommends measures at technical (tracing/offensive capabilities, early warning, backup networks, environment security), political (alliances, agreements, information-sharing), and societal (education, awareness) levels to reduce national security risks in smart cities.

title: Exploiting Smart City IoT for Disaster Recovery Operations
thesis: Smart city IoT infrastructure can be repurposed for military disaster recovery operations to enhance situational awareness, but integration raises security and interoperability challenges.
key_quotes: In the event of a natural disaster phenomenon such as an earthquake, the IoT devices within the city such as the traffic cameras, weather, and pollution sensors can be re-tasked to identify emergency conditions such as toxic gases in the air, people trapped in vehicles or rubble, or the status of the power grid. || Much of this work has been performed as part of a NATO Research Task Group (RTG) on Military Applications of Internet of Things (IST-147). || The interconnected smart city system can also constitute an additional attack surface on HADR applications – in fact a recent study has shown that many of the systems operated by cities are insecure or misconfigured.
policy_relevance: Recommends open standards, interoperability, and security measures (e.g., TPM, breaking-glass policies) for integrating civilian IoT with military HADR systems.

title: Algorithmic Surveillance and the Erosion of Privacy: Reconciling National Security and Human Rights in the Digital Era – A Comparative Study of the USA and UAE
thesis: This paper critically examines the regulatory, legal, and ethical implications of algorithmic surveillance in the UAE and USA, proposing a comparative framework for reconciling national security with human rights.
key_quotes: The rise of algorithmic surveillance in the United States and the United Arab Emirates presents profound challenges to privacy, due process, and human rights. || This paper critically examines the regulatory, legal, and ethical implications of algorithmic surveillance in both countries, proposing a comparative framework for reconciling national security imperatives with human rights protections. || the UAE’s centralized approach prioritizes security over privacy, while the U.S. emphasizes legal accountability and civil liberties despite technological challenges.
policy_relevance: Proposes a structured five-phase roadmap for AI governance: Pilot Sandbox & Risk Assessment, Legal Codification & Policy Framework, Institutional Capacity Building & Governance, Nationwide AI Deployment & Monitoring, and Continuous Evaluation & Legal Adaptation.

title: A Predictive Policing Application to Support Patrol Planning in Smart Cities
thesis: Presents ROTA-Analytics, a web-based predictive policing module that uses machine learning to forecast crime incidence and support patrol planning in Natal's smart city initiative.
key_quotes: ROTA-Analytics is a web-based application which aims to provide crime incidence forecasting as outputs. || This crime incident forecasting helps patrol supervisors to elaborate the list of predefined locations (points) and staying time at which each police vehicle must patrol. || The adoption of ROTA modules in the police activities has produced impressive strategic and operational results.
policy_relevance: None. The paper describes a technical system for police resource allocation but does not discuss broader policy implications or recommendations.

title: Leveraging Civilian IoT Infrastructures to Support Warfighting Activities in Urban Environments
thesis: Leveraging civilian Smart City IoT and Open Data infrastructures can support military HADR operations, demonstrated through a case study integrating SPF with Helsinki's Digitraffic service.
key_quotes: The increasing importance of urban environments in warfare, especially for counter-terrorism purposes, raises the opportunity to develop innovative military information systems that can easily integrate with civilian Smart City infrastructures and Open Data services to improve situational awareness. || The emergence of Open Data services, that expose both raw data collected from IoT installations in Smart Cities as well as processed information, raises the opportunity to consider integrating military systems with civilian ones in support of military operations in urban environments. || This paper presents an evaluation of the capabilities of SPF, the Fog-as-a-Service platform we designed for tactical environments, in supporting a hypothetical but realistic HADR mission in the Helsinki Smart City.
policy_relevance: None

title: Smart Cities as "Big Brother Only to the Dialogue Masses": The Limits of Personal Privacy and Personal Surveillance
thesis: Smart city projects processing only non-personal data still pose surveillance risks through securitizing logic that manages populations as aggregates, transforming public space into consumption space, and current data protection law fails to address this.
key_quotes: The idea behind this novel approach to smartness can be condensed into a statement offered by one of Stratumseind Living Lab’s actors: 'We are Big Brother only to the masses.' || As Foucault (2009: 4) put it: the overarching question of security is 'how to keep a type of (behaviour) within socially and economically acceptable limits and around an average that will be considered as optimal for a given social functioning.' || the securitizing logic of surveillance within the Stratumseind Living Lab and other smart cities is transforming public spaces into consumption spaces.
policy_relevance: Calls for adapting data protection law to address group privacy and the transformation of public space into consumption space; argues that privacy in public should protect political participation and sociability.

title: Privacy and Ethics in a Smart City: Towards Attaining Digital Sovereignty
thesis: Argues that smart city systems pose privacy and ethical challenges due to surveillance capitalism, advocating for digital sovereignty through regulatory principles and user control.
key_quotes: Fitness tracking app Strava gives away location of secret US army bases: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/jan/28/fitness-tracking-app-gives-away-location-of-secret-us-army-bases. || their cost for raw material is zero. They do not need to produce their product, i.e., information, it is being derived by running algorithms with a bare-bone minimum cost. || behavioral surplus had produced a stunning 3590% increase in revenue in less than four years for Google.
policy_relevance: Discusses GDPR principles (purpose specification, data minimization, transparency, data protection by design, impact assessment, consent) and Europe's AI Act as foundations for digital sovereignty; recommends continuous monitoring and inspection.

title: Das Polizieren der Zukunft
thesis: Predictive policing, as an application of Big Data, produces a narrative of unlimited control over the future that reinforces securitization of space, stereotyping, and the erosion of the presumption of innocence.
key_quotes: Predictive policing, in essence, is taking data from disparate sources, analyzing them and then using results to anticipate, prevent and respond more effectively to future crime. || Die Erzählung von Big Data ist vor allem eine Erzählung der unbegrenzten Planbarkeit, Kontingenzreduktion und Kontingenzbewältigung, eine Erzählung über mit hoher Wahrscheinlichkeit garantierbare Erwartungssicherheit und letztlich eine Erzählung über die Kontrollierbarkeit von Zukunft. || Daten gelten schließlich als wertfrei und moralisch neutral. Das sind sie aber keineswegs, weder in der Auswahl noch in der Auswertung und Interpretation.
policy_relevance: The paper critiques predictive policing for undermining legal standards (presumption of innocence) and reinforcing social inequalities, but does not offer specific policy recommendations.

title: Compliance-Industrial Complex: The Operating System of a Pre-Crime Society
thesis: The compliance-industrial complex, a hybrid of regulatory and surveillance capitalism, creates a pre-crime society through securitized, criminalized compliance that transfers state sovereignty to corporations and subjects individuals to algorithmic governance.
key_quotes: Compliance, as I argue, is fast becoming a new logic of governance, supported by the apparatuses of corporate security and private intelligence. || The compliance-industrial complex translates noble ideas into practices of control and pre-emption of future risks, into new forms of hybrid policing; it shapes the ways in which we are governed, profiled, sorted, surveilled, nudged, risk-assessed, punished, sanctioned—as workers, clients, customers, suppliers, and humans. || What we are dealing with here is not mere contractualization or outsourcing, but a privatization and pluralization of policing and the securitization of ethics at a more fundamental level.
policy_relevance: The paper critiques the current policy trajectory of anti-policies and securitized compliance, warning of the creation of a pre-crime society and the transfer of sovereign power to corporations. It calls for rethinking governance approaches to avoid the unintended consequences of algorithmic control and surveillance.

title: Dracula Urbanism and Smart City Mania: Urban Change in the Twenty-First Century
thesis: Smart city development is a Dracula-like force that reproduces inequality and spatial destruction through banal kill-offs, parasitic governance, and planetary operations.
key_quotes: The foundational afflicting act in smart developing we see across the globe: real-estate state kill-offs in cities. These actors quietly kill off the ways, activity spaces, and city presences of the supposedly degenerate in planning’s unbroken flow (the deemed toxic poor, anti-civic residents). || A banal eviscerating becomes an unexceptional thing, an end product of ordinary acts innocuously put in motion. || Dracula urbanism and its leading edge, smart developing, as a kind of banal postcolonial project.
policy_relevance: None

title: Remotely Piloted Aircrafts Toward Smart Cities
thesis: Remotely piloted aircraft (RPAs) are presented as versatile tools for smart city applications, with a case study of the SpaceVANT project in Natal, Brazil, developed through Triple Helix collaboration.
key_quotes: The SpaceVANT project was firstly conceived to support sounding rocket launch operations in CLBI. However, due to the many feasible uses and features that can be embedded to the platform, the project evolved to a wider view of applications. || The RPA emerges as an integrating vehicle of great importance in the development and sustainability of smart cities, being a vector for strengthening the innovation ecosystem covered in the Triple Helix (Universities, Governments and Industry) and used for the well-being of the Society, which is at the heart of the cities of the future. || RPAs can help track, trace, detect, and recognize criminals accurately. ... In a country of continental dimensions, thousands of terrestrial and fluvial borders, dense tropical forests and other geographical features that make it difficult to control territorial boundaries, may consider that the extensive use of RPA is a powerful security tool.
policy_relevance: Discusses Brazilian regulatory framework (ANAC RBAC-E no 94) for RPA operations and the need for aerodrome standards. Highlights Triple Helix collaboration as a model for innovation policy.

title: The Impact of Smart City Model on National Security
thesis: Smart city models, while improving quality of life, create significant national security threats through cyber vulnerabilities that can be exploited by state and non-state actors.
key_quotes: Smart cities could help overcome traditional problems of big cities, such as pollution, traffic congestion and administrative corruption. They can stimulate economic productivity, accommodate population growth, and make lives more convenient, but at the same time, they raise many security threats to national security. || If these services are targeted by a successful cyber-attack, the consequences in that case would be unaffordable to national security and to people’s lives. || Smart cities represent a lifestyle totally based on making use of such unprecedented technological developments as artificial Intelligence systems, the Internet of things and big data, with the aim of having high quality of life for people. However, they create several threats to national security, which make the smart city model questionable from security perspective.
policy_relevance: Recommends three levels of measures: technical (tracing/offensive capabilities, early warning, backup networks, environment security), political (alliances, agreements, information sharing), and societal (education, awareness, corporate responsibility) to reduce national security risks in smart cities.

title: Smart City Crime Prevention Services: The Incheon Free Economic Zone Case
thesis: This study analyzes the performance and limitations of smart crime prevention services in the Incheon Free Economic Zone, emphasizing the need for data accuracy, linkage, and specialized institutions.
key_quotes: The limitations of technology and equipment performance for smart security service operation... Collection sensitivity and frequent false alarms, due to the immaturity of the applied technology, have become a problem in the IFEZ smart security service. || The limitations of data linkage and tracking technologies were also observed... video data for confirming wanted vehicles and traffic conditions are in a format that only collects vehicle numbers by video and that does not allow such data to be processed into information that can continuously be used by the authorities. || Limitations to integrated data use among departments and organizations need to be addressed for smart city services. Integrated services like the smart city differ from existing digitization services focusing on single services and require the convergence of multiple departments and services.
policy_relevance: The paper recommends establishing consistent processes for data linkage, developing specialized institutions and experts, and improving technology performance to reduce false alarms and enhance data usability.

title: The Tragedy of Smart Cities in Egypt. How the Smart City is Used towards Political and Social Ordering and Exclusion
thesis: Smart cities in Egypt, particularly the New Administrative Capital, are used by political and military authorities as instruments of social and political ordering, exclusion, and segregation, not just for sustainable development.
key_quotes: Life in the NAC has a Janus face: on the one hand, inhabitants of the city have access to better services, modern smart infrastructure, first-class education and health care, and high-tech digital technologies; on the other hand, they are prisoners of the system with less freedom than many other citizens of the country. || The smart technologies are not used for civic participation, protection of civil liberties or crime prevention. They are rather used for data-driven policing and deep control. || The smart city can become an instrument to structure and organise society which may result in social exclusion and even effective segregation.
policy_relevance: The paper calls for research and debate on societal risks of smart cities, including misuse of cybernetic control, the 'terror of technology', and the smart city as a disciplinary strategy. It highlights the need for greater scrutiny of technology-driven urban governance.

title: Die „drohende Gefahr“ als Schlüsselbegriff einer Sekuritisierung des Rechts
thesis: The expanded concept of 'imminent danger' in German police law enables a securitization of law through preemptive control over time and space, exemplified by the endangerer figure, new police laws, and predictive policing.
key_quotes: Die Vorstellung von drohenden Gefahren im Sinne bloß vermutbarer, zukünftiger Gefahren noch diffusen Charakters wird im Polizeirecht und der polizeilichen Praxis immer verbreiteter. || Das eröffnet einem ‚governing through crime‘ (Simon) neuartige Möglichkeiten und lässt sich als Zeichen einer weitgefassten präventiven Sekuritisierung lesen, die nicht ohne totalitäre Gefahren ist. || Predictive policing produziert auf diese Weise eine Kriminogenisierung des Raumes, bei der die identifizierten Gebiete als permanente Risikoträger wahrgenommen werden; der Raum selbst steht unter Verdacht...
policy_relevance: The paper critiques the securitization of law through expanded police powers and calls for critical attention to the risks of preemptive control, but does not offer specific policy recommendations.

title: Prohibited AI surveillance practices in the Artificial Intelligence Act: promises and pitfalls in protecting fundamental rights
thesis: Evaluates the EU AI Act's prohibitions on AI surveillance, arguing that broad exceptions undermine fundamental rights protection despite expanded prohibitions.
key_quotes: The AI Act sets only partial prohibitions on the use of real-time remote biometric identification, predictive policing, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation systems, severely limiting their cope and allowing for a large number of exceptions. || The ECtHR concluded that the measures taken against the person concerned were particularly restrictive in view of his peaceful protest, which did not pose any threat to public safety. || The AI Act acknowledges the primary objective to protect fundamental rights as well as commits not to weaken the EU’s high data protection standards by stating that the AI Act should be without prejudice to existing EU law.
policy_relevance: Recommends that Member States implement fundamental rights-based approach, refrain from authorizing real-time biometric identification, and ensure effective enforcement mechanisms.

title: From Automation to Autonomy: Technological Sovereignty for Better Data Care in Smart Cities
thesis: Argues for DataCare model to implement technological sovereignty in smart cities, balancing urban data automation with citizen empowerment and ethical data governance.
key_quotes: Smart cities are a continuation of using tools—science and technology—as a mechanism to predict, control and shape urban environments. (p. 324) || Through the compression of time between data collection, interpretation, decision-making and intervention, as well as (false) claims to objectivity and neutrality, fully automated data-driven systems bypass and undermine the need for public deliberation and democratic control. (p. 326) || DataCare aims to increase data transparency and autonomy, showcase new business opportunities, and empower citizens and community. (abstract, p. 319)
policy_relevance: Proposes DataCare model as a practical framework for cities to implement technological sovereignty through data awareness, literacy, action, and futures scenarios. Recommends open standards, interoperability, and decentralised data architectures.

title: Trust and the Smart City
thesis: The smart city must be understood through the prism of trust and distrust, as trust is essential for the legitimacy and acceptability of urban digital governance.
key_quotes: The smart city lies somewhere between a material fact and an urban narrative. It is primarily material, in the sense that it refers to precise policy programmes and infrastructure associated with the digitalisation of public services. || For Ip and Cheng, such data and its related algorithms are not morally neutral (O’Neil 2016; Eubanks 2018; Susskind 2018). In their article, they argue that the development of smart cities could be morally problematic due to their pervasiveness, opacity, and diffused accountability. || Individuals usually have very little idea about how these algorithms work. In other words, residents of smart cities are living in a 'black-box society' (Pasquale 2015).
policy_relevance: The paper discusses the need for trust-building, ethical standardisation frameworks for smart city data, and attention to data security, confidentiality, and transparency to avoid exacerbating public distrust. It also notes the importance of coherent narratives around smart city initiatives.

title: Diving into the Iceberg: Establishing Transparency in AI for Law Enforcement
thesis: The paper argues that while the LED and AI Act together can enhance transparency in AI for law enforcement, structural limitations and practices of actors impede meaningful public scrutiny, especially in national security and predictive policing.
key_quotes: Clearview AI’s operations highlight key issues surrounding the intersection of AI technologies, data protection regulations, and law enforcement practices. On one hand, personal data protection frameworks such as the GDPR serve as a crucial safeguard against the misuse of technologies like facial recognition. On the other hand, the effectiveness of these frameworks is often contingent on individual awareness and the ability to exercise rights such as the right to information and the right of access. || The right to information and of access provide an important step to reveal the tip of an iceberg. However, structurally the LED provides 'individualist claims subject to individualist remedies', and cannot correspond to effects of AI technologies at a population-level. || Both the LED and the AI Act fail to lift the 'veil of secrecy' surrounding national security data practices, which obstructs collective governance and delays accountability for individuals challenging AI use in national security.
policy_relevance: Recommends harmonizing transparency obligations across security actors, narrowing national security exceptions, and incorporating transparency obligations into police legislation and criminal procedural frameworks to ensure public scrutiny.

title: A serious game empowering the prediction of potential terrorist actions
thesis: This paper introduces a serious game to generate training datasets for reasoning algorithms that predict terrorist actions in urban environments.
key_quotes: The main value proposition of all the above systems is the effective coverage and surveillance of large urban areas in a way that minimises the number of human resources (e.g. patrolling policemen/officers) required. || The anticipation of terrorist actions could allow Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) to proactively deal with them thereby minimising their adverse effects. || The development of systems for predicting potential terrorist attacks hinges on devising appropriate reasoning and analytics techniques that could operate over information collected from various sources, including sensor sources, human operators and open source information (OSINT).
policy_relevance: None beyond suggesting the game as a tool for LEAs to improve threat prediction and resource allocation.

title: Studying Surveillance AI-cologies in Public Safety: How AI Is in the World and the World in AI
thesis: Proposes the concept of 'surveillance AI-cology' and a methodology for studying AI surveillance in public safety through a quintuple helix and ELSA framework, illustrated with a Living Lab in Scheveningen.
key_quotes: Using AI in public safety might carry the increased risk of contributing to opaque decision making, structural inequalities, and the further manifestation of systemic injustices. || The general intention to turn the boulevard into a venue that is more attractive to 'upscale tourism' might influence the definition of suspicious patterns and pre-emptive intervention. || Surveillance AI-cologies are made up of interconnected collections of disparate actors (technological, human, more-than-human, organisational, etc.), all implicated in AI-aided surveillance tasks.
policy_relevance: Recommends systematic inclusion of ELSA and quintuple helix stakeholders in AI surveillance development, and calls for democratic control, public engagement, and investment in democratic infrastructure.

title: Automating Crime Prevention, Surveillance, and Military Operations
thesis: Automation in crime prevention, surveillance, and military operations changes knowledge production, power dynamics, and fundamental rights, requiring critical analysis.
key_quotes: The central thesis of the chapter is that automation is changing knowledge production and creating new language in crime and social control and potentially impacting the already delicate process of the re-distribution of power by influencing elections and indirectly the constitutional framework of a given society. (Završnik & Klobasa, Ch. 1) || Mathematics helped invent new concepts such as 'meaning extraction', 'sentiment analysis', 'opinion mining', and 'computational treatment of subjectivity in text'. (Završnik & Klobasa, Ch. 1) || Algorithms do not only make visible by reproducing an otherwise inaccessible reality... Algorithmic vision produces a reality from which to act, a reality filled with blind spots, inaccurate objects, and biases. (Hogue, Ch. 10)
policy_relevance: The book implies a need for regulation, transparency, and human rights safeguards in the use of automation in criminal justice and military operations, but does not offer specific policy recommendations.

title: Smart cities and the architecture of security: pastoral power and the scripted design of public space
thesis: Smart city technologies use pastoral power through behavioral scripting (light, sound, smell) to secure public space, moving from exclusion to inclusion.
key_quotes: we show that the securitisation of urban space can also be pursued by positive triggers for behaviour. || the architecture of security is now a 'scripted architecture': the design of public space to introduce defaults for desirable behaviour by using non-physical elements of the built environment, such as light, smell and sound. || The focus in this form of pastoral architecture is on inclusion rather than exclusion, on positive rather than negative incentives, and on psychological mechanisms of behaviour rather than physical deterrence.
policy_relevance: The paper critiques the depoliticized nature of smart city initiatives and highlights the role of private companies in shaping urban governance, urging policymakers to consider the political implications of behavioral scripting and public-private partnerships.

title: Big Data, Crime and Social Control
thesis: Examines the legal, ethical, and social implications of big data analytics in crime and social control, highlighting challenges to civil liberties, democracy, and social justice.
key_quotes: The new mathematical language serves security purposes well... the mathematical sciences offer a grammar of combinatorial possibilities that allows for things – people, objects and data – to be arranged together, for links to be made. || The homeland security apparatus has successfully lobbied for extraordinary funding... But when it comes to striking at the heart of terror financing... the prerogatives of financiers and the secretive wealthy trump homeland security concerns. || The goal of framelessness: that of total information capture.
policy_relevance: Discusses need for regulatory solutions, judicial oversight, and best practices to address privacy, discrimination, and accountability in big data-driven crime control.

title: Tweets of surveillance: Traffic, Twitter, and securitization in Beirut, Lebanon
thesis: The Twitter account for Beirut's Traffic Management Center serves as a portal to view how the state secures its legitimacy through surveillance and securitization of urban space, while also being a site of contestation by citizens.
key_quotes: the surveillance camera represents the cool efficiency and capacity for precision associated with technology (p.329) || the regulatory logic of these 'tweets of surveillance' is one that encourages self-regulation (p.330) || In a militarized urban landscape, one territorialized by divisive political claims situated within a volatile geopolitical context (p.333)
policy_relevance: None explicitly discussed, but the paper calls for greater ethnographic engagement with smart urbanism in the Global South and highlights the tensions and possibilities of these technologies.

title: Smart Cities and Their Impact on the Colombian Navy
thesis: Smart city concepts and technologies can enhance the Colombian Navy's operational capabilities, reduce technological dependence, and foster innovation.
key_quotes: Maritime security and surveillance: Through the implementation of technologies for real-time tracking and monitoring detection, maritime security of suspicious activities can be improved. || It promotes the development of R&D projects, not only in officers but also in sailors in training, through their degree projects and research workshops. || collaborative work and transfer of knowledge and technology
policy_relevance: None

title: Prohibited AI surveillance practices in the Artificial Intelligence Act: promises and pitfalls in protecting fundamental rights
thesis: The EU AI Act's prohibitions on AI surveillance practices are partial and contain broad exceptions, failing to fully protect fundamental rights from mass surveillance and predictive policing.
key_quotes: The AI Act aims to prohibit unacceptable AI practices which contradicts EU values of respect for human dignity, freedom, equality, democracy and the rule of law and fundamental rights enshrined in the Charter, including the right to non-discrimination, to data protection and to privacy and the rights of the child (recital 28). || The AI Act sets only partial prohibitions on the use of real-time remote biometric identification, predictive policing, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation systems, severely limiting their cope and allowing for a large number of exceptions. || The ECtHR noted that national legislation lacks detailed rules governing the scope and application of measures relating to the use of facial recognition technology. It also considered that there was a lack of safeguards against the misuse and abuse of those technologies.
policy_relevance: The chapter critically evaluates the EU AI Act's prohibitions on AI surveillance, highlighting gaps and exceptions that may undermine fundamental rights. It recommends that Member States fully endorse a fundamental rights-based approach, refrain from introducing new AI surveillance tools, and implement effective enforcement mechanisms.

title: Digitalisation of public administration under martial law in Ukraine and the case of Smart City Kyiv
thesis: Examines the digitalisation of public administration in Kyiv under martial law, highlighting the dual-use of smart city technologies for civilian governance and wartime security.
key_quotes: The Air Alarm application was created to provide additional information about the situation in different regions of the country. This unique case became an alternative to the outdated street notification system. || The chatbot e-Vorog has become a powerful tool of public intelligence. || During the war, the Reserve+ application appeared – an electronic office where information about the status of conscripts and reservists could be obtained.
policy_relevance: Proposes legislative unification (adoption of a Smart City Law), public consensus, technological development, information campaigns, and scientific approach to digitalisation. Emphasises post-war reconstruction using smart city concepts.

title: Responsible civilian drones
thesis: Civilian drones, due to their military origin, pose dual-use risks and raise fundamental human rights concerns, requiring citizen involvement in design.
key_quotes: There is always the risk of ‘dual use’: where functionality in one domain may be useful in other domains as well and where this other use may be counterproductive. || It is important to keep the military origin of drones in mind when considering their use in a non-military, civilian, context. || there is the risk of dual use: drones have a military origin, and this technology is now being further used and developed in a civilian setting. The values embodied in these technologies do not automatically reflect societal needs.
policy_relevance: Discusses EU U-space regulation and the need for citizen involvement in co-designing drone services to address privacy and security concerns.

title: Integrating digitization into public administration: Impact on national security and the economy through spatial planning
thesis: Digitization in spatial planning creates dual-use security risks, as civil urban technologies can be repurposed for military purposes and smart cities introduce vulnerabilities threatening national security.
key_quotes: Every level of digital technology serves two purposes: first, it creates a digital space where security is also required, leading to the formation of cybersecurity, information security, network security, and digital infrastructure; second, it reinforces and ensures security (e.g., a unified system of video surveillance cameras that allows for real-time recording of threats and taking appropriate actions to eliminate them). || Understanding how the collaboration between spatial planning/development experts and military experts developed and then broke down in Los Angeles in particular demonstrates how a shared understanding of the rapidly growing urban crisis as a national security crisis helped to turn urban planning concerns into strategic challenges that needed to be addressed by deploying techniques and technologies of command, control, computers, communications, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance. || The dense smart city infrastructure reframes the city for its residents as a 'platform for services'.
policy_relevance: Recommends that integrating digitization into public administration within spatial planning must consider impacts on national security and the economy, and that city administrators should set clear boundaries for partnerships with defense communities.

title: Urbicide in Israel’s War on Gaza: Architecture of Erasure and the Unmaking of Urban Life (2023–2025)
thesis: Urbicide in Gaza is a deliberate strategy of spatial erasure and home unmaking within settler-colonial warfare, not merely collateral damage.
key_quotes: urbicide—the deliberate killing of the city as a living space—has emerged as a defining feature of asymmetric and settler-colonial conflicts. || the erasure of infrastructure, housing, and essential services served not only as a means of military incapacitation but as a deliberate strategy to dismantle Gaza as a space of urban life, memory, and sovereignty. || Hospitals, schools, mosques, media institutions, and universities have been struck under the rationale of dual-use or symbolic alignment with resistance.
policy_relevance: None explicitly, but calls for further research on post-urbicidal recovery, politics of memory, and spatial justice.

title: The atrocities of war leave profound impacts
thesis: Urbicide in Palestine is a systematic, intentional destruction of urban space using architecture and planning as tools of colonial control and military domination.
key_quotes: The military elites did not traverse the city using conventional roads or public spaces but created alternative routes through the urban fabric, a strategy we term 'forced routes' or 'walking through walls.' || I term 'design by destruction'. This manipulation turns our professional skills into tools for enforcing dominance, illustrating a stark misuse of urban planning and architectural design. || It was more than I could bear to think of them using our bathrooms, opening my drawers, and misplacing our clothes or personal items.
policy_relevance: Calls for decolonizing knowledge and universities, and for recognizing urbicide as a war crime or crime against humanity similar to genocide.

title: The Threat Posed by Commercial First- Person View (FPV) Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) Modified by Asymmetrical Warfare Actors
thesis: Commercial off-the-shelf UAVs are easily modified by non-state actors for asymmetric warfare, posing an existential threat that requires understanding their design, operation, and countermeasures.
key_quotes: Distinctions between 'civilian and military' have now virtually vanished; with the 'war-fighting footprint' changing such that there are no defined battlefronts, nor distinguishable combatants. || Technology is inherently dual-use using commercial inertial navigation units, found in toy helicopters and Wii controllers, ideal for indigenous modification. || Unfortunately, 'Dual-use cannot be legislated against. How do you prevent lines of code from a civilian coder being used in military items?' || UtD implementation isn't just about platform acquisition, it is rather a revolutionary transformation of digital products, combining sensors' inputs, with information architecture to exploit the potential of real-time UAV operations.
policy_relevance: Advocates for pre-sale legislative action and design modifications (e.g., omitting weapon mounting points, increasing radar reflectivity) to limit exploitation. Discusses UK Parliamentary inquiry on domestic threat of drones and need for counter-drone systems.

title: Western Fantasy and Tropical Nightmare: Spectacular architecture and urban warfare in Rio
thesis: Spectacular architecture and mega-events in Rio de Janeiro are intertwined with urban warfare, forced evictions, and racial violence, creating a pattern of uneven development and control termed 'riofication'.
key_quotes: Control and its technologies are imported or created locally and have turned the old capital of Brazil into a testing ground for new forms of apartheid and intensive population control, under a dystopian regime. || From the occupied territories of Palestine under high-tech spatial and vertical domination to the hills and slums of Rio, there continues to be an intense exchange of occupation and control tactics, territorial advancement strategies, weapons and drones. || The Museum of Evictions, a landscape of the ruins of forced displacement, has a special meaning when the future does not look promising for the vast majority of the population.
policy_relevance: None

title: Spatialization of oppression: Contemporary politics of architecture and the urban
thesis: Architecture and urban space are active political forces that produce oppression, spectacle, and control through data, media, and spatial violence.
key_quotes: The excessive production of big data, made possible and supported by 'algorithmic governmentality' ('big data' usually means anything that can be digitized and recorded), conceals who is making profit from it and hides the level of surveillance that it enables. || What we lose as a result of this algorithmic governmentality, Mattern argues, is the exposure to alterity, something that was easily accessible and possible when one wandered physically through a city. || For architecture and the urban to have relevance in the 21st Century, we cannot merely reignite the approaches of thought and design that were operative in the last century... architecture and urban space should be understood as political forces in and of themselves.
policy_relevance: None explicitly stated; the chapter calls for rethinking architecture and urban space as political forces, but does not offer specific policy recommendations.

title: Concentration of Urban Violence in Fortaleza and Strategies for Crime Prevention
thesis: Spatial analysis of violent crime concentration in Fortaleza shows strong correlation with socio-economic vulnerability and urban disorder, enabling targeted resource allocation for crime prevention.
key_quotes: The results demonstrate how locations characterized by high levels of violence are spatially correlated with more vulnerable locations in terms of both socio-economic-demographics and urban disorder. || There is a spatial association between violent crimes and aggregate sectors of strong vulnerability in the city, which was confirmed by the statistical correlation between the SVI and the different components of the RAI. || Applications of evidence-based policing, data-driven policies, and community-oriented strategies to reduce crime have hitherto primarily been conducted in the United States and other Western-industrialized cities, but they could also find fertile ground in Latin America.
policy_relevance: Proposes targeted crime prevention strategies combining ostensible policing, community policing, urban infrastructure improvements, and social capital fostering in 124 identified high-risk micro-territories, based on cost-benefit analysis for resource allocation.

title: Disappearing Palestine: Israel's Experiments in Human Despair
thesis: Israel's systematic dispossession and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians aims to erase Palestine and its people through legal, military, and bureaucratic means.
key_quotes: Israel has turned the increasingly confined spaces left to the Palestinians not only into open-air cages but also into laboratories where experiments to encourage Palestinian despair, and ultimately emigration, are being refined. || The gradual ethnic cleansing of the Palestinians from their homeland, on both sides of today's Green Line, is likely to take place with few witnesses to record it. || The purpose of the tower-and-stockades 'was to change the map of eretz Israel by erecting new settlements, to make it as difficult as possible to solve the problems of this land by means of division or cantonization.'
policy_relevance: Calls for international recognition of Palestinian rights and an end to support for Israeli occupation; advocates for a reappearance of Palestine and its people.

title: Urban Violence and Militarization
thesis: Cities and violence are mutually constitutive; contemporary urban militarization blurs military-domestic lines through technology transfer and surveillance.
key_quotes: Drones have been marketed – and used – for policing within the US: what Wall and Monahan (2011) call a 'drone stare' has moved from Afghan and Iraqi warzones into US cities. || There has also been a militarization of urban policing through drawing on military surveillance technology and techniques for policing uses. || moves to allow military agencies notionally targeting those 'outside' the state to increasingly conduct surveillance domestically, and for policing agencies 'inside' to work with military agencies 'outside' in order to access intelligence on citizens.
policy_relevance: Argues against excessive militarization and surveillance in response to urban violence; advocates for responses that build urban community and resist fear (e.g., 'we're not afraid' campaign).

title: Leviathan's Architect: Urbicide, Urban Renewal, and the Right to the City in Turkish Kurdistan
thesis: Post-conflict razing and reconstruction in Turkish Kurdistan securitizes urban space, displaces Kurds, and imposes state designs, but also sharpens Kurdish identity and agency.
key_quotes: The act of urbicide—literally, killing the city—erodes Lefebvre's right to the city both as a participatory oeuvre and as a schedule of enumerated freedoms. || The state has harnessed tabula rasa reconstruction for its own ends, displacing and dispossessing residents as it seeks to remake the physical as well as social fabric of Kurdish-majority cities. || The upheaval has been disorienting for residents, but in other ways it has sharpened Kurdish identity and agency.
policy_relevance: The paper calls for a new political language for planning and design that hinges on history and inclusion rather than Realpolitik, and highlights the need for accountability for civilian deaths and the protection of cultural heritage.

title: Wargaming and the Just War
thesis: Wargaming can contribute to analyzing just war considerations, especially with AI in urban warfare, but current wargames often omit civilian elements needed for ethical evaluation.
key_quotes: Battles today are increasingly being fought within urban environments, where King (2021) and others see that the density of people and infrastructure, and concepts such as smart cities challenge the prosecution of war. || Urban conflicts offer new challenges as to how they should be wargamed (Burden, 2023a) and how to keep war just, and the USECT model provide one potential framework to help in this. || Unfortunately, most wargames do not represent the civilian population to any meaningful degree (Burden, in press).
policy_relevance: None

title: Robowar™ dreams: US military technophilia and global south urbanisation
thesis: Critically examines US military's technophiliac efforts to adapt its Revolution in Military Affairs to urban warfare in global south cities, warning of automated, robotized warfare.
key_quotes: The first key effort to redirect the RMA to the purported challenges of US forces attempting to dominate and control global south cities involves programmes designed to saturate such cities with myriads of networked surveillance systems. || The overwhelming rhetoric in such efforts emphasises that new military techno-science, specifically developed to address cities, will turn global south urban environments into areas that US forces can completely dominate, using their technological advantages, with minimum casualties to themselves. || The central challenge of CTS, according to DARPA, will be to build up fully representative data profiles on the 'normal' time-space movement patterns of entire subject cities so that algorithms could then use statistical modelling to 'determine what is normal and what is not'.
policy_relevance: None explicitly, but implies need for critical scrutiny of military urban research and the dangers of autonomous weapons.

title: Time-series satellite remote sensing reveals gradually increasing war damage in the Gaza Strip
thesis: High-resolution satellite imagery and deep learning enable near real-time detection and quantification of escalating war damage to buildings, infrastructure, and agricultural land in the Gaza Strip.
key_quotes: In this study, we define urban annihilation by aerial or artillery bombardment as the systematic destruction of buildings, critical infrastructure and cultural heritage within conflict areas, which manifests as significant changes in the urban landscape detectable and measurable via high-resolution satellite imagery. || We found that 15.4% of structures were destroyed, 18.7% severely damaged, 11.8% moderately damaged and 12.5% slightly damaged. || The LuoJia3-01 satellite data are crucial for impartial conflict monitoring, and our innovative methodology offers a cost-effective, scalable approach to assess future conflicts in various global contexts.
policy_relevance: The paper calls for an immediate ceasefire and highlights the methodology's potential for impartial conflict monitoring, UXO risk assessment, and post-conflict reconstruction planning.

title: Urbicide in Israel’s War on Gaza: Architecture of Erasure and the Unmaking of Urban Life (2023–2025)
thesis: Urbicide in Gaza (2023-2025) is a deliberate strategy of spatial erasure and home unmaking, not collateral damage, serving settler-colonial domination.
